page: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and dedicated fourth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8488C processors running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance configuration features 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core on an x86_64 architecture. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 105 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware-level acceleration flags include AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution units, and cryptographic suites such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 16.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 5000 MHz, providing a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. Network throughput is provisioned at a 3 Gbps baseline without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and the configuration contains zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation shows robust CPU execution metrics, highlighted by top-quartile results in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.73 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing scoring 2743.0. General CPU operations fall within middle-tier expectations, recording 1899.38 in single-core and 7550.03 in multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 7695.0 and PassMark CPU score of 13119.77. In-memory throughput reflects 47.98 GB/sec read and 44.81 GB/sec write bandwidth on large blocks, though PassMark memory tests registered in the lower quartile.

This hardware profile delivers efficient compute density for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive RAM pools or local NVMe scratch disks. It is appropriately aligned with workloads such as web application serving, batch data processing, continuous integration and build pipelines, and moderate caching layers like Redis, while larger model inference is constrained by core memory ceilings.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based virtual server engineered for CPU-intensive processing tasks. Built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C platform operating at 3.2 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores paired with 16.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory. The instance features vector acceleration including AVX-512 and AMX instructions, alongside a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect consistent middle-tier compute and memory performance, with standout results in single-threaded gzip compression and text parsing. With its 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio, the c7i.2xlarge represents a resource-balanced compute environment for CI/CD compilation, static web serving, containerized application clusters, and batch data processing where dedicated per-core compute capacity is prioritized over large local memory footprints.
